<source_mitigation_status/> <source_notes/> <source_recommendation><![CDATA[In order to properly restrict your application's behavior, a Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header should be created. At a minimum, this header should limit access to outside content by specifying a tightly constrained 'default-src' value.
Unfortunately, there is no universal setting for this value because it must to be tailored to your application. It should be as restrictive as possible without disrupting the functionality of your application. The best way to determine this is to start with the Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only (CSPRO) header given a 'default-src' value of 'self'. This will report any time an external source is loaded by your application. Using this output, you will be able to tune the allowed default sources to include those which your application legitimately needs.
Once the base sources have been determined, the header should be changed from CSPRO to CSP, thereby restricting external content from being rendered within your application. ]]></source_recommendation> <source_references/> <source_remediation_status>Reported</source_remediation_status> <source_request/> <source_resolved_date>2025-07-20 15:51:24</source_resolved_date> <source_response/> <source_sdlc_status/> <source_severity>5</source_severity> <source_target_fix_date/> <source_vulnerability_explanation><![CDATA[We observed 2 pages which did not set the Content-Security-Policy header. The last violations of this policy are listed as follows:]]></source_vulnerability_explanation> <source_vulnerability_summary><![CDATA[Content-Security-Policy is an opt-in site protection mechanism supported by current browsers. It can be used to tightly restrict the content and behavior of the page. Adding restrictions can greatly reduce the attack surface of the page.
It is used to restrict from where various HTML elements can be sourced, to where the page can communicate, and how the page can identify itself. Not setting Content-Security-Policy header allows the browser to assume the application trusts content loaded from external domains. This means it will attempt to render elements and execute scripts from any source, including those which are unknown and potentially malicious. ]]></source_vulnerability_summary> <state>1</state> <state_inheritance_count>0</state_inheritance_count> <steps_to_reproduce/> <substate/> <sys_class_name>sn_vul_app_vulnerable_item</sys_class_name> <sys_created_by>VR.System</sys_created_by> <sys_created_on>2025-07-20 15:51:24</sys_created_on> <sys_domain>global</sys_domain> <sys_id>043a2522c37ea650fc40382a050131bb</sys_id> <sys_mod_count>1</sys_mod_count> <sys_updated_by>VR.System</sys_updated_by> <sys_updated_on>2025-07-20 15:51:26</sys_updated_on> <technical_details/> <ttr_applied_rule/> <ttr_calculated>false</ttr_calculated> <ttr_status>no_target</ttr_status> <ttr_target_date/> <use_ttr>true</use_ttr> <vulnerability display_value="Contrast Security CWE - 602">309edc8797e222106b73be6de053af25</vulnerability> <vulnerable_links>https://teamserver-staging.contsec.com/Contrast/static/ng/index.html#/119844af-42ff-4293-b06b-81d426e9a4a9/applications/9c9d2333-e4d2-437c-90c2-68221ee774ad/vulns/VQI7-2AGY-4GME-ERAV</vulnerable_links> <vulnerable_method_info/> <work_notes/> </sn_vul_app_vulnerable_item> </record_update>
